Revised assessment incorporating the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS):
- Tone: Still balanced-to-cautiously hawkish given the hold at a restrictive rate and ongoing balance-sheet runoff, with vigilance on inflation and acknowledgment of policy-lag risks.
- SLOOS overlay tilts risk to the downside: Banks reported broad-based tightening across C&I and CRE, as well as most consumer categories (residential mortgages, HELOCs, auto, subprime, other consumer), alongside tighter terms (higher loan rates, wider spreads, lower LTVs, higher DSCRs). Reasons cited include the economic outlook, funding costs, deposit outflows, liquidity positions, collateral values, and credit quality. Foreign banks also tightened spreads and expect further C&I tightening; many banks expect to continue tightening.
- Demand backdrop: Weaker loan demand for C&I (plant/equipment, M&A, inventory, A/R), while card demand was unchanged but with tighter terms. These survey results align with and reinforce the FOMC’s statement that tighter credit will weigh on activity, hiring, and inflation.
- Net: While labor-market strength and policy backstops help, SLOOS points to persistent and broad credit headwinds, suggesting downside risks to growth and an earlier deceleration in inflation pressure. Relative to the FSR-only read, the SLOOS moves sentiment from slightly positive toward neutral-to-slightly negative.
